$comment: A TextMate grammar for ASN.1 value notation. Shared with asn1-docs, which uses it to colour schema listings. Highlighting says whether text looks like ASN.1. Whether it is a correct profile is what euicc check says.
name: asn1-vn

comment-line.comment: X.680 12.6.3: a line comment ends at a newline or at a second --
comment-line.name: comment.line.double-dash.asn1

hexstring.comment: X.680 12.12: an hstring denotes a value, not text. Quotes around it make it look like a string, and calling it one put 30 per cent of a real profile in the colour of prose -- next to the 39 per cent that are member names, which the Dark 2026 theme paints #9CDCFE against #A5D6FF for a string. Two thirds of a file in one indistinguishable blue. As a numeric constant it is #B5CEA8 in every default theme, which is also what it is.
hexstring.name: constant.numeric.hex.asn1

binstring.comment: X.680 12.11: a bstring, and a value for the same reason.
binstring.name: constant.numeric.binary.asn1

assignment-head.comment: X.680 16.1: valuereference Type ::= Value. The reference is lower case and the type upper case, which is grammar and not convention. It is left uncoloured on purpose: it is module syntax around the value and not part of it, and euicc steps over it when reading. Listed before #alternative and #fieldname, which would otherwise claim the reference, since all three match at the same offset and the earlier rule wins.

typeref.comment: X.680 12.2: a type reference begins with an upper case letter. The lookbehind matters: a hyphen is a word boundary, so a plain \b let this match Mandatory-services inside the field name eUICC-Mandatory-services, and the editor coloured half an identifier as a type.
typeref.name: entity.name.class.asn1

fieldname-first.comment: The first word on a line, which in a value is a member name. #fieldname needs a value after the name to know it is one, so a name stayed the colour of nothing until the next word was typed, and half of writing a profile happened in white. A line begins a member often enough to settle it on its own. The lookahead hands a CHOICE alternative back to #alternative, which cannot win otherwise: this rule starts at the indent, further left, and the leftmost match is the one TextMate takes.

alternative.comment: X.680 29.2: an alternative of a CHOICE is written `name : value`. It selects one of a fixed set rather than naming a slot every value has, which is what an enum member is, so it takes that scope and the brighter blue #4FC1FF that themes give one. The colon is what tells the two apart, and it is the same distinction euicc has to make when reading.
alternative.name: variable.other.enummember.asn1

fieldname.comment: A member name inside a value. Value notation is an object literal from top to bottom, so these carry the scope a theme colours an object literal key with: TypeScript gives meta.object-literal.key and the default dark theme paints it #9CDCFE. Without this rule almost every line of a profile is white, because almost every word in one is a member name. A name that is itself the value, an ENUMERATED identifier, is followed by a comma or a closing brace, so the lookahead leaves it plain, the way an identifier used as a value stays plain in TypeScript.
fieldname.name: meta.object-literal.key.asn1
